drafted_by: AI, requires clinician review before any real use.

questions.text: What is the main problem: headache, neck pain, a lump in your neck, sore throat, hoarse voice, ear problem, or sinus symptoms?
questions.rationale: Clarifying the main complaint guides the next branch of the interview.

questions.text: Did the headache come on suddenly and reach its worst within a minute, or build up over time?
questions.rationale: Thunderclap onset raises concern for subarachnoid hemorrhage.

questions.text: Where is the headache, what does it feel like, and how often do you get it?
questions.rationale: Location and pattern help separate tension, migraine, cluster, and secondary headaches.

questions.text: Do you get nausea, sensitivity to light or sound, or visual aura with the headache?
questions.rationale: Associated features support migraine.

questions.text: Do you have fever together with neck stiffness, light sensitivity, or a rash?
questions.rationale: This combination raises concern for meningitis.

questions.text: Do you have weakness, numbness, trouble speaking, vision loss, double vision, or confusion with the headache?
questions.rationale: Focal neurologic symptoms suggest stroke or other intracranial pathology.

questions.text: Have you hit your head recently, especially if you take blood thinners?
questions.rationale: Recent head trauma, especially with anticoagulation, raises risk of intracranial bleeding.

questions.text: Are you over 50 with a new headache, scalp tenderness, jaw pain when chewing, or vision changes?
questions.rationale: This pattern suggests giant cell arteritis, which can cause blindness if untreated.

questions.text: Is your neck pain from an injury, and does it spread into your arm or cause numbness?
questions.rationale: Mechanism and radiation help separate strain from radiculopathy or fracture.

questions.text: Have you found a lump in your neck? How big is it, how long has it been there, and is it painful?
questions.rationale: Painless persistent neck masses raise concern for malignancy, while tender nodes suggest infection.

questions.text: Has the lump grown steadily, felt hard or fixed, or have you had weight loss or night sweats?
questions.rationale: These features raise concern for lymphoma or head and neck cancer.

questions.text: How long has your throat been sore, and is it one-sided, severe, or worse when swallowing?
questions.rationale: Severity and laterality help separate viral pharyngitis, strep, and peritonsillar abscess.

questions.text: Are you drooling, unable to swallow saliva, or have a muffled 'hot potato' voice?
questions.rationale: These findings suggest peritonsillar abscess, epiglottitis, or deep neck infection.

questions.text: Do you have noisy breathing, difficulty breathing, or a feeling that your throat is closing?
questions.rationale: Airway compromise is an emergency.

questions.text: Have you been hoarse for more than three weeks?
questions.rationale: Persistent hoarseness, especially in smokers, needs laryngeal evaluation.

questions.text: Do you have trouble swallowing solids or liquids, or does food get stuck?
questions.rationale: Dysphagia can indicate esophageal, throat, or neurologic disease.

questions.text: Do you have ear pain, drainage, or a feeling of fullness?
questions.rationale: Otalgia and discharge point to otitis externa or media.

questions.text: Have you lost hearing, especially suddenly, or have ringing in the ear?
questions.rationale: Sudden sensorineural hearing loss is time-sensitive for treatment.

questions.text: Do you have facial pressure, nasal blockage, thick discharge, or loss of smell?
questions.rationale: These are typical features of rhinosinusitis.

questions.text: Do you have nosebleeds, how often, and how long do they last?
questions.rationale: Frequency and duration guide the assessment of epistaxis.

questions.text: Is there swelling or redness around your eye, or pain moving your eyes?
questions.rationale: Orbital cellulitis can complicate sinus infection and is an emergency.

questions.text: Do you smoke, chew tobacco, or drink alcohol regularly?
questions.rationale: Tobacco and alcohol are major risk factors for head and neck cancer.

questions.text: When did this start, and is it getting better, worse, or staying the same?
questions.rationale: Onset and trajectory help distinguish acute from chronic problems.

questions.text: Do you take pain relievers frequently, blood thinners, or any new medicines?
questions.rationale: Medication overuse headache and anticoagulation change risk and management.

questions.text: What is the main thing you are worried this could be?
questions.rationale: Understanding the patient's concern guides reassurance and follow-up questions.

red_flags.label: Sudden worst headache
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient describe a headache that came on suddenly and severely, the worst of their life?

red_flags.label: Fever with stiff neck or light sensitivity
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report fever together with neck stiffness, photophobia, confusion, or a non-blanching rash?

red_flags.label: Neurologic symptoms with headache
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report weakness, numbness, speech trouble, vision loss, or confusion with the headache?

red_flags.label: Head injury on blood thinners
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report a recent head injury, especially while taking anticoagulants, with worsening symptoms?

red_flags.label: Possible giant cell arteritis
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient over 50 report new headache with scalp tenderness, jaw pain on chewing, or visual changes?

red_flags.label: Airway compromise
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report drooling, muffled voice, stridor, or difficulty breathing or swallowing saliva?

red_flags.label: Suspicious neck lump
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient describe a hard, growing, or persistent neck lump with weight loss or night sweats?

red_flags.label: Sudden hearing loss
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report hearing loss that came on suddenly over hours to days?
